question_text: How does the Strategy pattern differ fundamentally from the State pattern, despite sharing similar UML class diagrams?

options.text: Strategy pattern objects are aware of each other and handle transitions; State objects are isolated
Strategy encapsulates interchangeable algorithms chosen by the client; State encapsulates state-dependent behaviors and drives automatic transitions
Strategy applies only to asynchronous operations; State applies to synchronous calls
State pattern requires compile-time polymorphism; Strategy is purely dynamic

answer_explanation: In Strategy, clients generally configure the context with an algorithm strategy. In State, the context's behavior changes dynamically based on internal state changes.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: In Strategy, clients generally configure the context with an algorithm strategy. In State, the context's behavior changes dynamically based on internal state changes.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
